newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Flemings says upgrades Czech equities to neutral.
newsitem.headline: Flemings says upgrades Czech equities to neutral.

text.p: The research arm of investment bank Robert Fleming Securities has upgraded its outlook on the Czech equities market to neutral from underweight, a Flemings research report to investors said.
The report said that Czech equities have substantially underperformed against other major eastern European markets within its Europe/Middle East/Africa portfolio.
"The PX50 index is now fairly valued on a forward PER (price earnings ratio) to December 1998 of less than 11 times," the report, written on August 15, said.
"This adequately compensates for the risk of unpleasant earnings surprises arising from this summer's devaluation (of the crown)," it added.
The PX50 index closed at 538.8 on Friday, down some 19 percent for 1997 and on Monday lost 6.3 points on jitters from last week's sharp drop on Wall Street.
The report said the underperformance was in part due to a currency crisis with the crown in mid-May, emergency tightenings of monetary fiscal policy and corporate earnings downgrades.

At the end of May, the crown, under heavy short-selling pressure by foreign hedge funds, was forced out of its +/-7.5 percent daily fixing band. The central bank now allows the currency to float freely.
The report said the crown crisis appeared to be nearing an end, and that there are "early signs of adjustment in the real economy to the devaluation and fiscal austerity packages are encouraging".
"The natural stocks on which to focus are export earners. However, Czech quoted equities provide relatively low exposure to the export sector," the report said.
"The most interesting vehicles are Ceska Zbrojovka, DEZA, Galena, Skoda Plzen, and ZPS Zlin," it added.
